 Open Navigation Menu Menu Culture Latest OTT releases (November 2-November 8): 15 new movies and TV shows on Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar and more
 Looking to add to your watchlist? Mihir Ahuja sparks chaos during a holiday gathering in Dilwali Diwali , and a visually impaired Saif Ali Khan races to identify a vengeful killer played by Akshay Kumar in Haiwaan By Prabal Sharma 2 November 2026 Saif Ali Khan in Haiwaan It'’s time for your weekly update of the latest OTT releases and the next seven days have the perfect blend of movies and TV shows to satiate all your bingeing needs. Mihir Ahuja finds himself in a generational clash during a tense holiday gathering in the family drama Dilwali Diwali ; a visually impaired man ( Saif Ali Khan ) relies on his remaining senses to outsmart a vengeful murderer (Akshay Kumar) in the thriller Haiwaan ; The Greatest chronicles the athletic triumphs and political activism of boxing legend Muhammad Ali; Keira Knightley balances covert assassinations with her husband’s rising political career in Black Doves season 2; Owen Wilson returns to the amateur golf circuit as washed-up former professional Pryce Cahill in Stick season 2.
 Bass Machina (November 3) 
 Brian Tyree Henry, Tati Gabrielle and Janelle Monáe lend their voices to this adult animated steampunk Western created by LeSean Thomas. Set on a lawless frontier overrun by supernatural terrors and rogue technology, the story follows an ageing gunslinger who serves as judge, jury and executioner to protect his family. The six-episode limited series explores the personal costs associated with maintaining order in a violent, mechanical wilderness.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 A Dog’s Perfect Christmas (November 4) 
 Kicking off the streaming platform's holiday season lineup, this family feature stars Dennis Quaid and adapts another popular W. Bruce Cameron novel. The plot centres on a family that begins spiralling out of control during the holiday celebrations until a resourceful stray puppy arrives and forces the fractured relatives to cooperate.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Stick season 2 (November 4) 
 Owen Wilson returns as washed-up former professional golfer Pryce Cahill for the second season of this sports comedy series. The new episodes continue exploring the complex dynamic between Pryce and his teenage prodigy Santi Wheeler (Peter Dager), as they navigate the highly competitive amateur circuit. The ensemble cast includes Marc Maron, Rhea Seehorn and Judy Greer as the characters balance their sporting ambitions against their personal failures.
 Streaming on Apple TV 
 Taken: Natalee Holloway (November 4) 
 This three-part documentary series reexamines the highly publicised 2005 disappearance of 18-year-old American student Natalee Holloway during a graduation trip to Aruba. Directed by Dani Sloane and Matthew Galkin, the production features never-before-seen archival footage and exclusive access to the initial investigators. The series details the immediate timeline of her disappearance while heavily documenting her family’s subsequent pursuit of criminal justice across international borders.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Greatest (November 4) 
 This new biographical series chronicles the life and cultural impact of boxing legend Muhammad Ali. The narrative covers his initial rise through the heavyweight ranks while focusing on his political activism, religious conversion and subsequent exile from the sport. The series attempts to contextualise his athletic achievements within the broader social and political turbulence of the 1960s and ’70s.
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 Dilwali Diwali (November 5) 
 Directed by Ritesh Menon, this family drama centres on a young man ( Mihir Ahuja ) who returns home for the festival of lights and sparks a messy collision of generational expectations and emotional revelations. Produced by Terribly Tiny Tales, the cast features Manoj Pahwa and Neelu Kohli navigating the complicated dynamics of an extended family gathering.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Black Doves season 2 (November 5) 
 Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw return as the streaming platform’s most stylish pair of assassins for the second season of this British spy thriller. The new episodes pick up with Helen Webb continuing to hide her lethal profession from her husband, a deception made significantly more difficult as he prepares to become the next Prime Minister. The season explores the escalating tension of operating a covert network while sitting directly in the political spotlight.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 North of North season 2 (November 5) 
 The Canadian comedy returns to the tight-knit Arctic community of Ice Cove just as winter sets in. The second season follows Siaja, an ambitious young Inuk mother, as she attempts to prove to her boss that she is capable of far more than managing a simple calendar. The production balances the humour of small-town northern life with the emotional weight of Siaja’s shifting personal priorities.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 One Year to Live, Buy a Man (November 5) 
 Adapted from the popular webcomic, this romantic Japanese feature makes its global digital premiere. The narrative focuses on a young woman who, after receiving a terminal diagnosis with only one year left to live, decides to use her remaining savings to financially support a struggling aspiring actor in exchange for company and entertainment. The film tracks how their transactional arrangement rapidly evolves into a genuine emotional connection during her final months.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Haiwaan (November 6) 
 Directed by Priyadarshan, this thriller serves as an official remake of the 2016 Malayalam film Oppam . Saif Ali Khan stars as a blind caretaker who discovers a dead body and immediately becomes the prime suspect in the murder investigation. He must rely entirely on his heightened remaining senses to identify the real culprit, a vengeful killer played by Akshay Kumar, and clear his own name before the police officially close the case.
 Streaming on SonyLIV 
 Meesaya Murukku 2 (November 6) 
 Hiphop Tamizha Adhi reprises his starring role in this sequel to the 2017 Tamil musical comedy, arriving on streaming just in time for Diwali. The plot follows Jeeva, an aspiring musician whose personal life becomes deeply complicated when a powerful film producer’s son takes a romantic interest in his partner, Laila. The ensuing conflict forces Jeeva to uncover his family’s buried musical history, with Adhi playing multiple roles across different generational timelines.
 Streaming on SonyLIV 
 Nooru Kodi Vaanavil (November 6) 
 Harish Kalyan and Siddhi Idnani star in this Tamil romantic drama directed by Sasi. Skipping a traditional theatrical run, the long-delayed project makes its direct digital premiere. The narrative centres on a young couple attempting to navigate a romance tested by contrasting familial expectations and grounded everyday struggles. The plot focuses on the emotional weight of their relationship and the personal sacrifices the protagonist must make to keep their connection intact against mounting external pressures.
 Streaming on ZEE5 
 Possible Love (November 6) 
 Acclaimed South Korean director Lee Chang-dong returns after an eight-year hiatus with this new drama feature. The narrative follows two married couples—a laid-off worker and his wife, alongside a documentary filmmaker and her husband—whose lives intersect during a film project. The script focuses on their contrasting outlooks and hidden desires as they navigate their shifting emotional landscapes.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Under Siege (November 6) 
 Netflix debuts an eight-part Colombian limited series based on the harrowing true events of the 1985 Palace of Justice takeover. On November 6, 1985, the M-19 guerrilla commando unit forcibly entered the building, taking over 300 people hostage, including Supreme Court justices. The series recreates the initial assault, the military’s subsequent recapture of the building the following day, and the decades-long legal battles pursued by the victims’ families.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Institute season 2 (November 8) 
 This sci-fi thriller based on Stephen King’s novel returns for its sophomore season. Following the explosive events of the first instalment, Luke and Tim continue their struggle against the clandestine organisation that abducts psychic children to use as human batteries for precognitive predictions. With the introduction of the mysterious operative Nolan Reeves, played by Alfie Allen, the new episodes raise the stakes as the protagonists attempt to dismantle the remaining operational facilities.
 Streaming on MGM+ via Prime Video
